cards.front: light source
cards.back: Something that makes its own light, such as the Sun, a lamp or a candle.
cards.say: light source. Something that makes its own light, such as the Sun, a lamp or a candle.

cards.front: dark
cards.back: Where there is no light, or very little light.
cards.say: dark. Where there is no light, or very little light.

cards.front: reflect
cards.back: When light bounces back off an object, such as from a mirror.
cards.say: reflect. When light bounces back off an object, such as from a mirror.

cards.front: shadow
cards.back: A dark shape made when an object blocks light.
cards.say: shadow. A dark shape made when an object blocks light.

cards.front: Which is a light source: the Sun or the Moon?
cards.back: The Sun. The Moon only reflects light from the Sun.
cards.say: Which is a light source: the Sun or the Moon? The Sun. The Moon only reflects light from the Sun.

cards.front: Which is a light source: a torch or a mirror?
cards.back: A torch.
cards.say: Which is a light source: a torch or a mirror? A torch.

cards.front: Is a candle a light source?
cards.back: Yes. A burning candle makes light.
cards.say: Is a candle a light source? Yes. A burning candle makes light.

cards.front: Is a book a light source?
cards.back: No. A book does not make light.
cards.say: Is a book a light source? No. A book does not make light.

cards.front: Name a light source in the sky.
cards.back: The Sun. Stars are also light sources.
cards.say: Name a light source in the sky. The Sun. Stars are also light sources.

cards.front: Name a light source made by people.
cards.back: A lamp, a torch or a candle.
cards.say: Name a light source made by people. A lamp, a torch or a candle.

cards.front: Why can we see things in the day?
cards.back: The Sun gives light, and the light bounces off things into our eyes.
cards.say: Why can we see things in the day? The Sun gives light, and the light bounces off things into our eyes.

cards.front: Why can we not see in a dark room?
cards.back: There is no light for things to bounce into our eyes.
cards.say: Why can we not see in a dark room? There is no light for things to bounce into our eyes.

cards.front: What do we need to see an object?
cards.back: Light.
cards.say: What do we need to see an object? Light.

cards.front: What does a mirror do to light?
cards.back: It reflects light, so we can see an image.
cards.say: What does a mirror do to light? It reflects light, so we can see an image.

cards.front: Why do cats' eyes shine in the dark?
cards.back: They reflect light. They are not light sources.
cards.say: Why do cats' eyes shine in the dark? They reflect light. They are not light sources.

cards.front: How is a shadow made?
cards.back: When an object blocks light.
cards.say: How is a shadow made? When an object blocks light.

cards.front: When is your shadow longest?
cards.back: In the early morning or late afternoon.
cards.say: When is your shadow longest? In the early morning or late afternoon.

cards.front: When is your shadow shortest?
cards.back: At midday, when the Sun is high.
cards.say: When is your shadow shortest? At midday, when the Sun is high.

cards.front: Can you have a shadow in the dark?
cards.back: No. A shadow needs light.
cards.say: Can you have a shadow in the dark? No. A shadow needs light.

cards.front: Why should you never look straight at the Sun?
cards.back: Its light is so bright that it can hurt your eyes.
cards.say: Why should you never look straight at the Sun? Its light is so bright that it can hurt your eyes.

cards.front: What gives us light when the power goes out?
cards.back: A torch or a candle.
cards.say: What gives us light when the power goes out? A torch or a candle.
